I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the cropping pattern I trust most because it fits the climate, the irrigation conditions, and the way I know how to manage risk. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will focus on topdressing, one or two timely irrigations if moisture is short, and disease and insect control only when pressure shows up. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or miss the best sowing window. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because the yield is usually better and the stand is stronger. I will keep fertilizer moderate rather than excessive, because costs matter and too much nitrogen can cause lodging or wasted money. I will use rotary tillage after harvest because it is practical for me and matches local machinery service. This plan gives me stable grain, manageable labor, and lower production risk over the whole year.
